source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐν τῇ Τεσσαρακοστῇ ἄρτον προσφέρειν, εἰ μὴ ἐν Σαββάτῳ καὶ Κυριακῇ μόνον.
thought_title: Offering bread only on Sabbath and Lord's Day in Lent
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its canons, and this canon regulates when the Eucharistic offering of bread may be made during Lent.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary in Lent to offer bread, except on Sabbath and on the Lord's Day only.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'offering' for προσφορά, and the verb προσφέρειν with ἄρτον refers to the Eucharistic offering of bread; 'offer bread' keeps the literal sense.
The standard rendering of Κυριακή for Sunday in early Christian texts; keeps the literal sense of 'belonging to the Lord'.
δεῖ expresses necessity or obligation; the negation means 'it is not required' or 'one must not', and 'it is not necessary' preserves the impersonal force.

pass_b_english: During Lent one must not to offer bread except on the Sabbath and the Lord's Day only.

problems.why: οὐ δεῖ means 'it is not right/proper' or 'one must not', expressing prohibition, not mere lack of necessity.
problems.fix: During Lent one must not offer bread except on the Sabbath and the Lord's Day only.

fixed: Changed 'it is not necessary' to 'one must not' because οὐ δεῖ expresses prohibition, not lack of necessity.

last_rejected.why: προσφέρειν here means offer the Eucharist, not merely 'offer bread'
last_rejected.ruling: ἄρτον προσφέρειν literally means 'offer bread'; Eucharistic sense is contextually implied but not lost by literal rendering.
